I spent four hours last Tuesday trying to figure out why our invoice job was writing duplicate rows. The answer turned out to be embarrassing. A retry wrapper someone added in 2023 had no idempotency key, so any timeout during the third-party call produced a second write, and timeouts were common on Fridays because the vendor ran their own batch jobs then.

Nobody had noticed for two years. The duplicates were small, a few dozen a month, and they got cleaned up by a reconciliation script that everyone assumed was doing something else entirely.

What bothers me is not the bug. It's that we had two systems papering over each other, and the only reason I found it was that I happened to be reading logs for an unrelated reason.

I don't have a clean lesson here. "Add idempotency keys" is true and useless; we knew that. The real question is how you find the seams where one workaround is quietly covering for another, and I still don't know the answer.
